`process.exit()` stops the process at once. Work that is still pending is dropped, `finally` blocks do not run, and the code that called yours gets no chance to handle the failure. Throw an error instead, or set `process.exitCode` and let the process end when it has nothing left to do.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
function loadConfig(path) {
  if (!exists(path)) {
    console.error("config not found");
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
function loadConfig(path) {
  if (!exists(path)) {
    throw new Error("config not found");
  }
}
```

The rule allows `process.exit()` in three places. A file that starts with `#!` is a command-line program, which decides for itself when to end:

{/* good */}
```js
#!/usr/bin/env bun
if (!(await run())) {
  process.exit(1);
}
```

A handler passed to `process.on()` or `process.once()`:

{/* good */}
```js
process.on("SIGINT", () => {
  closeServer();
  process.exit(130);
});
```

And a file that imports something from `node:worker_threads`, where `process.exit()` ends the worker thread and not the process:

{/* good */}
```js
import { parentPort } from "node:worker_threads";

parentPort.on("message", message => {
  if (message === "stop") process.exit(0);
});
```
